title: feat(ui): add AdaptiveCompactDatePicker
body:
A field showing the selected date that opens the calendar on tap, sharing AdaptiveDatePickerState with the inline picker so the selectable-dates rule applies unchanged.

- Material: an outlined button opens a DatePickerDialog that edits a scratch state, so the shared state only changes on confirm; dismiss or tapping outside discards the pick
- iOS: the system compact UIDatePicker, which pops its calendar over the content. Bounds coming from a DateBounds apply natively; the control cannot grey out days any other rule rejects, so such a pick snaps to the nearest selectable day
- iOS: DatePickerManager gains presentations (inline, wheels, compact), an enabled flag and an intrinsic size that is measured again after each selection because the compact label resizes
- iOS: the state-to-native sync composable is shared by the inline and compact pickers, and native pickers are keyed on their state so taps never reach a stale instance
- Tests: AdaptiveCompactDatePickerMaterialTest (desktopTest, Compose UI, incl. picking a day in the dialog)
- Docs: compact picker section; sample gains a compact section

title: feat(ui): add AdaptiveDateRangePicker
body:
A range picker with its own AdaptiveDateRangePickerState: one common class wrapping Material3's DateRangePickerState on every platform, with the same selectable-dates rule as the single-date pickers. The Material3 state is wrapped so it reports the caller's rule object, which keeps the Material3 picker in sync when the rule changes.

- Material: the Material3 DateRangePicker. It scrolls its months and cannot take an unbounded height, so inside a scrolling column it falls back to DateRangePickerFallbackHeight instead of crashing
- iOS 16+: a native UICalendarView with multi-date selection driven by a pure DateRangeSelection reducer (first tap sets the start, a tap on or after it sets the end, a tap before it moves the start, any tap on a complete range starts over); every day of the range is highlighted and rejected days are greyed out. Below iOS 16 the Material3 picker is shown
- iOS: the UICalendarView setup, including the refresh of visible days after rule changes, moves into a CalendarViewHost shared by the single-date and range calendars
- Tests: DateRangeSelectionTest (commonTest) and AdaptiveDateRangePickerStateTest (desktopTest, incl. rendering inside a vertically scrolling column and a live rule change)
- Docs: range picker section; sample gains a range section

title: feat(io): add KmpFile.source() for streaming reads with kotlinx-io
body:
Closes #537.

Large picked files could only be read with readByteArray(), which loads them fully into memory; on Android getPath() returns a content URI, so there was no way to stream them at all.

- calf-io now depends on kotlinx-io (api) and exposes `suspend fun KmpFile.source(context): kotlinx.io.RawSource` plus a context-free overload next to the other KmpFile extensions
- Android opens the content URI through ContentResolver, iOS and desktop go through SystemFileSystem, JS/Wasm buffer the file in memory because browsers have no synchronous reads
- kotlinx-io 0.9.1 added to the version catalog
- Docs: "Streaming with kotlinx-io" section in docs/filepicker.md, including the okio bridge via kotlinx-io-okio
- Sample: file picker screen streams each picked file in 64 KB chunks
- Tests: KmpFileSourceTest (calf-io desktopTest, 6 tests)

title: Prepare 0.14.0: Kotlin 2.4.20, Compose 1.12.0, AGP 9.4, compileSdk 37
body:
## Summary

**0.14.0 is published** (release run [34748782626](https://github.com/MohamedRejeb/Calf/actions/runs/34748782626)). This PR brings `main` up to date with the release branch: latest Kotlin / Compose Multiplatform, AGP 9 with the new KMP Android library plugin, compileSdk 37, and a green CI.

### Toolchain

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Kotlin | 2.4.10 | **2.4.20** |
| Compose Multiplatform | 1.11.1 | **1.12.0** |
| Material3 (CMP table) | 1.11.0-alpha07 | **1.12.0-alpha03** |
| JetBrains Navigation (sample, CMP table) | 2.9.2 | **2.10.0-alpha02** |
| AGP | 8.13.2 | **9.4.0** |
| compileSdk | 36 | **37** |
| Gradle | 9.0.0 | **9.7.1** (AGP 9.4 needs ≥ 9.6) |
| kotlinx-datetime / Coil / Ktor / Vanniktech / kyant | | 0.8.0 / 3.6.2 / 3.5.2 / 0.37.0 / 2.0.1 + 1.2.1 |

Companion versions follow the CMP 1.12.0 release-notes table.

### AGP 9 migration

AGP 9's new DSL no longer allows `com.android.library` + `org.jetbrains.kotlin.multiplatform` in the same subproject, so:

- All `calf-*` modules (and `sample:common`) now use **`com.android.kotlin.multiplatform.library`** via the convention plugin. `androidTarget()` / `android.library.gradle.kts` are gone; the target is configured in `Android.kt` (`kotlin { android { } }`, single variant, published through the regular KMP publication). `withHostTest {}` keeps `commonTest` running on the Android JVM (`testAndroidHostTest` is part of `allTests`).
- The hierarchy template matches the AGP target explicitly: KGP's `withAndroidTarget()` is an `instanceof KotlinAndroidTarget` check that silently excluded `materialMain` from the Android compilation.
- `sample:android` uses AGP's built-in Kotlin (no `org.jetbrains.kotlin.android` plugin, no `kotlinOptions`), drops the obsolete manifest `package` attribute.
- Dropped dead `gradle.properties` flags (`kotlin.mpp.androidSourceSetLayoutVersion`, `kotlin.mpp.androidGradlePluginCompatibility.nowarn`, `kotlin.js.compiler`) and the Gradle 9.6-deprecated `by registering` task DSL.

### Behaviour notes

- **Library minSdk stays 23.** androidx navigation 2.10+ declares minSdk 24, so `calf-navigation` keeps androidx navigation at 2.9.7. Only the sample app moves to minSdk 24 (JetBrains navigation 2.10's Android artifact requires it).
- Web targets declare `binaries.executable()`: CMP 1.12 fails `jsBrowserTest`/`wasmJsBrowserTest` otherwise (`checkComposeUiTestConfigurationFor*`, CMP-4906). Published klibs are unchanged.
- CI runners move from `macos-14` to `macos-26`: CMP 1.11+ links against iOS 26 SDK frameworks (`UIUtilities`), which is why `main` is currently red (`linkDebugTestIosSimulatorArm64`: "framework 'UIUtilities' not found").

## Test plan

- [x] `./gradlew assemble` – all modules, all targets (Android AAR, desktop, iOS arm64 + simulator, JS, Wasm) and all sample apps (Android debug/release APK, desktop, web, iOS frameworks)
- [x] `./gradlew allTests` – desktop (80 tests), Android host (32), JS + Wasm browser, iOS simulator; all green
- [x] CI (`Java CI with Gradle`) green on this PR (build job 20 min on macos-26)
- [x] `deploy.yml` dispatched with `0.14.0` from `0.14.x` completed successfully (run 34748782626: build, native libs, publish to Maven Central, version bump). The automated bump commit was fast-forwarded onto this branch and its PR #547 closed as a duplicate.

title: Fix file picker export and getPath; add onError, bookmarks and web save dialog
body:
## Description

Fixes four file picker bugs found while building Save As in Annodoc. Also adds a few things picked up from comparing Calf with FileKit, which are cheap to add before 1.0.0.

### Bug fixes

- **Android save wrote a 0-byte file.** The bytes or file to save were held in a plain `remember`, which was lost while the save sheet was open. They now live in `rememberSaveable`, so a file source also survives process death. The created document gets a real MIME type from its extension, writes use mode `"wt"`, and a failed write deletes the empty document.
- **iOS export name had a `<UUID>-` prefix** (cherry-pick of `2145426`). Staged files now go into `tmp/<area>/<UUID>/<name>`, so the sheet offers the requested name.
- **iOS export moved the source file** (also from `2145426`). The export sheet now uses `asCopy = true` and says "Save", not "Move".
- **`KmpFile.getPath()` wasn't a filesystem path on mobile.** It now returns a decoded filesystem path or `null`:
  - Android returns a path only for `file:` URIs; content URIs give `null`.
  - iOS returns the path of the readable copy.
  - The new `KmpFile.toUriString()` gives the URI that `getPath()` used to return.
- **iOS swipe-dismiss mid-animation was never reported.** A shared `DocumentPickerDelegate` handles both delegate protocols and reports the result exactly once.
- **iOS picked copies lost their names.** Picked files keep their original names.
- **Android didn't report a missing documents app.** An `ActivityNotFoundException` now goes to `onError` instead of crashing.

### New API

- **`onError: (FilePickerException) -> Unit`** on `rememberFilePickerLauncher` and `rememberFileSaverLauncher`, on every platform. The old overloads stay and delegate: the picker ignores errors, and the saver reports `null` as before.
  - If some picked files can't be read, `onError` fires once, then `onResult` gets the files that could be read.
- **`FilePickerSettings(initialDirectory: KmpFile?)`** opens dialogs in a folder the user picked. On iOS this uses `directoryURL`.
- **New `KmpFile` functions:**
  - `KmpFile.fromUriString(…)` rebuilds a file from `toUriString()` or from an absolute path.
  - `getSize()` and `getMimeType()`.
- **Bookmarks:** `createBookmark()`, `KmpFile.fromBookmark(…)` and `releaseBookmark()` keep access to picked files across restarts.
  - Android persists URI permissions.
  - iOS stores a bookmark and holds security-scoped access on the resolved URL until release (FileKit #667).
  - Desktop stores the absolute path; the web has no bookmarks.
- **Web save dialog:** the saver uses `showSaveFilePicker` where the browser has it (Chromium), and falls back to `<a download>` in Safari and Firefox.

### Behaviour change

`getPath()` on Android and iOS no longer returns a URI string. If you relied on that, switch to `toUriString()`. `docs/filepicker.md` has a migration note.

## Related Issue

None on GitHub. These were reported from Annodoc's Save As work.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [x] Improvement
- [x] Documentation update
- [x] Build/CI change (Robolectric + Compose UI test deps for Android host tests)

## Platforms Tested

- [x] Android: host tests (Robolectric), plus a manual pass on a Pixel 9 emulator (API 35)
- [x] iOS: simulator unit tests, plus a UI pass on an iPhone 17 Pro simulator (iOS 26.2), driven with XCUITest
- [x] Desktop: unit tests
- [x] Web: the Wasm sample in a Chromium browser, with `showSaveFilePicker` stubbed (see below)

### Tests added

- **calf-io:**
  - Desktop: path, metadata and bookmark tests.
  - iOS: path (7), metadata (6), bookmark (4).
  - Android: `KmpFile` (8), bookmark (5).
- **calf-file-picker:**
  - Android: saver launcher (10), picker launcher (4), initial directory (2).
  - iOS: picker delegate, staging, initial directory, `stagePickedUrls`.
  - Desktop: initial directory, partial-failure message.

### Android emulator pass

- [x] Export writes a valid 374×374 PNG (32,417 bytes), stored as `image/png`.
- [x] Cancelling the save sheet reports a cancel.
- [x] A picked file shows `null` from `getPath()` and a content URI from `toUriString()`, plus the right size and MIME type, and can be read as a stream.
- [x] A folder bookmark holds a persisted read+write grant, which is still there after the app's process is killed.

### iOS simulator pass

- [x] The save sheet offers `profile_picture` (extension hidden by the sheet) and says "Save", not "Move". The file lands as `profile_picture.png`, a valid 318×318 PNG, and the saver's staging folder is emptied.
- [x] Swiping the save sheet down reports "Save cancelled", both after it settles and while it is still sliding in. Swipes 40–200 ms after the sheet starts appearing, in 20 ms steps, were all reported; none dismissed silently.
- [x] With a picked folder as the initial directory, the picker opens in that folder. That holds even after a pick from another folder, which moves the system's remembered location. After Reset, it follows the remembered location again.
- [x] A file picked there shows its original name, a readable-copy path (`tmp/calf-file-picker/<UUID>/notes.txt`), `25 bytes · text/plain`, and streams.

The iOS 26 save sheet has no Cancel button; swiping down is how it is dismissed.

### Web pass (Wasm sample, Chromium, save picker stubbed)

- [x] Save: Calf calls `showSaveFilePicker` with `suggestedName: profile_picture.png` and an `image/png` / `.png` type, writes the PNG (1,073 bytes) and reports "Saved successfully".
- [x] Cancel (`AbortError`) reports "Save cancelled".
- [x] A refused picker (`SecurityError`, e.g. no user gesture) falls back to a download of `profile_picture.png`.
- [x] Without `showSaveFilePicker` (Safari, Firefox) the file is downloaded, and its blob URL is still readable 2 s after the click.

### Still to check

- [ ] Chrome's own save dialog by hand (the stub covers Calf's side only).
- [ ] Safari: Export Photo downloads the file.

## Checklist

- [x] Builds successfully on all targeted platforms
- [ ] Verified UI behavior across at least one mobile and one desktop target (Android and iOS done; desktop UI not checked by hand)
- [x] Updated documentation/examples if the API or usage changed
- [ ] Confirmed no breaking changes without proper deprecation notice (`getPath()` on mobile changes meaning, see above)
